note: Tooltips (short and expanded) are the add-in's own public UI text. Split-button parents carry an internal id and no command of their own. Expanded tooltips added 2026-11-03 (second inventory run).

commands.label: ACC Gate
commands.tooltip: Runs project-wide actions on live ACC cloud models: opens each selected model, applies the actions, synchronizes changes and closes it — model after model, in one run. Works without an open model.
commands.tooltip_expanded: Select the models from the project's Model Registry and choose the actions — among them creating and repairing cloud links from the Link Matrix, worksets, standard schedules, sheets, materials, families, shared coordinates, PDFs and health checks. One combined run log documents every model. Needs your APS credentials (APS Settings).

commands.label: ZenLinks
commands.tooltip: Adds selected cloud models as links to the active model, with the settings the project's Link Matrix prescribes — the single-model counterpart of ACC Gate's cloud linking.
commands.tooltip_expanded: 1. Pick a Model Registry CSV and check the model(s) to link. 2. Pick the Link Matrix that documents their settings. The registry choice is remembered — hold Ctrl while clicking to pick a different one. The Link Matrix is always asked for.

commands.label: Link from Registry
commands.tooltip: Adds selected cloud models as links to the active model, with the settings the project's Link Matrix prescribes — the single-model counterpart of ACC Gate's cloud linking.
commands.tooltip_expanded: 1. Pick a Model Registry CSV and check the model(s) to link. 2. Pick the Link Matrix that documents their settings. The registry choice is remembered — hold Ctrl while clicking to pick a different one. The Link Matrix is always asked for.

commands.label: Export Cloud Link Matrix
commands.tooltip: Creates the project's Cloud Link Matrix from the Model Registry — one governed record of which models link into which hosts, with which settings. ACC Gate builds and repairs the cloud links from it.
commands.tooltip_expanded: One row per host and link model, with default worksets and link settings to adjust before use.

commands.label: ZenRegistry
commands.tooltip: Reads the active cloud model's project and model IDs and adds a ready-made row to the project's Model Registry — the model list ACC Gate and the link tools work from.
commands.tooltip_expanded: The active model must be an ACC / BIM 360 cloud model.

commands.label: Cloud GUIDs
commands.tooltip: Reads the active cloud model's project and model IDs and adds a ready-made row to the project's Model Registry — the model list ACC Gate and the link tools work from.
commands.tooltip_expanded: The active model must be an ACC / BIM 360 cloud model.

commands.label: ZenPrintPdf
commands.tooltip: Exports PDFs from the active model as defined in the PrintJobs sheet of its Print Intel workbook — no print dialogs, no PDF printer needed.
commands.tooltip_expanded: • Select the workbook Export Print Intel produced • Pick one output folder — it applies to every job • Every filled-in row becomes one combined PDF • Leave PdfSetupName blank to use the ZEN default

commands.label: Print PDF
commands.tooltip: Exports PDFs from the active model as defined in the PrintJobs sheet of its Print Intel workbook — no print dialogs, no PDF printer needed.
commands.tooltip_expanded: • Select the workbook Export Print Intel produced • Pick one output folder — it applies to every job • Every filled-in row becomes one combined PDF • Leave PdfSetupName blank to use the ZEN default

commands.label: Export Print Intel
commands.tooltip: Exports an Excel workbook describing the active model's print setup. Its PrintJobs sheet is where you define the PDFs for Print PDF.
commands.tooltip_expanded: One workbook, five sheets: • Worksets, Links, PrintSets — reference data from the model • PrintJobs — fill in PrintSetName per row, then run Print PDF • ModelInfo — identifies the model for ACC Gate batch printing

commands.label: Import Worksets
commands.tooltip: Applies a workset standard from a CSV to the active model: missing worksets are created, existing ones kept. The model must be workshared; the CSV isn't tied to a Revit version.
commands.tooltip_expanded: ACC Gate applies the same standard to many cloud models in one run (Create Worksets From Registry).

commands.label: Sheets
commands.tooltip: The sheet-list standard: export the SHEET LIST schedule, or create and rename sheets from a CSV — in this model or many local files.

commands.label: Import Sheets
commands.tooltip: Creates or renames sheets in the active model from a CSV — column A sheet number, column B sheet name. The CSV isn't tied to a Revit version.
commands.tooltip_expanded: Close the CSV in Excel before running.

commands.label: Batch Import
commands.tooltip: Creates or renames sheets from one CSV in many local Revit files in one run, without opening each file yourself. For cloud models, use ACC Gate.
commands.tooltip_expanded: Same CSV format as Import Sheets; the CSV isn't tied to a Revit version.

commands.label: Export Authority CSV
commands.tooltip: Captures the project's shared-coordinate position from the active model as a Coordinate Authority CSV — the reference every model of the project is aligned to.
commands.tooltip_expanded: Apply it with Apply Authority CSV, or to many cloud models at once with ACC Gate's Acquire Shared Coordinates action.

commands.label: Apply Authority CSV
commands.tooltip: Sets the active model's shared-coordinate position from a Coordinate Authority CSV and writes a before/after log. Doesn't save or sync — review the result first.
commands.tooltip_expanded: The CSV isn't tied to a Revit version: an authority exported in one Revit year applies in another. ACC Gate's Acquire Shared Coordinates action applies it to many cloud models.

commands.label: Export Schedule Definitions (WB)
commands.tooltip: Captures how the standard schedules are built — fields, filters, sorting and grouping — in a workbook that isn't tied to a Revit version, so schedule standards can be governed without keeping a source Revit file. Step 1 of 2.
commands.tooltip_expanded: Then use Import Schedule Definitions (WB) to rebuild the schedules in any model — no source Revit file needed. Appearance (fonts, colors, grid lines) isn't included in this version; for a full copy use Import Schedules (RVT).

commands.label: Import Schedule Definitions (WB)
commands.tooltip: Rebuilds the standard schedules in the active model from a workbook made with Export Schedule Definitions (WB) — no source Revit file needed, and the workbook isn't tied to a Revit version. Step 2 of 2.
commands.tooltip_expanded: For a full copy including appearance, use Import Schedules (RVT) with a source Revit file instead.

commands.label: Import Schedules (RVT)
commands.tooltip: Copies the standard schedules, with their view templates, from a source Revit file into the active model — a full copy, including appearance.
commands.tooltip_expanded: The source file must be from the same or an older Revit version. For a version-free route, use the Schedule Definitions (WB) pair.

commands.label: Batch Import (RVT)
commands.tooltip: Copies the standard schedules from one source Revit file into many local Revit files in one run.
commands.tooltip_expanded: The source file must be from the same or an older Revit version than the target files.

commands.label: Monitor & Swap
commands.tooltip: Switches a project to a renamed family library in one pass: every placed instance of an OLD_… family moves to the matching NEW_… family and type, after you review each pair.
commands.tooltip_expanded: Saves re-placing or re-typing instances by hand when a family naming standard changes. Families are paired by name after the prefix, types by equal type name. Afterwards the old families can be purged.

commands.label: Type Marks by Family
commands.tooltip: Assigns numbered Type Marks (for example DOOR-050, DOOR-051) to all types of the families whose names contain a search term, starting from a number you choose.
commands.tooltip_expanded: Run it once per category with its own number range — for example doors from 0, windows from 50, walls from 100. The search term becomes the mark's prefix.
